description: A single Board of Directors member card: a circular B&W headshot, or an initials-avatar fallback when the member has no photo, plus name and role. Shared by the landing BoardOfDirectors section and isolated scenarios.
name: BoardMemberCard

description: The 'Connect With Us' social footer from the live chapter pages: a centered heading, the contact email, and the social links rendered as dark circular icon badges. Reads the editable socials + contact email from the settings singleton and reuses socialIconSrc + buildMailto.
name: ChapterConnect

description: Per-chapter "Upcoming Events in {city}" section. Takes an already-filtered, sorted list of upcoming events for one chapter and renders them as shared EventCards; renders nothing when the list is empty so a chapter with no events shows no empty block.
name: ChapterEvents

description: Full-bleed city header for a chapter page (mirrors the live harvardintech.com pages): a background photo with a dark overlay and centered light 'HARVARD IN TECH <CITY>' title plus tagline. Falls back to the centered ChapterHeader when heroImage is absent.
name: ChapterHero

description: A single regional chapter page recomposed to match the live harvardintech.com chapter pages: a full-bleed ChapterHero, a ChapterSignUp band, the narrow content block (back link + ChapterLeads + markdown body slot + ChapterLinks), an optional EventGallery (showGallery), and a ChapterConnect social footer. Reused by the /chapters/[slug] route and isolated scenarios.
name: ChapterPage

description: Entry-point page for /chapters/<slug>. Enumerates the chapters content collection via getStaticPaths and renders each chapter through ChapterPage inside BaseLayout. getStaticPaths is also the one place holding both the full chapters list and the full events list, so it is where unmatchedChapterTags runs: any event whose chapter tag matches no chapter is named in a single console.warn visible in the Actions build log and under astro dev. The warning is advisory only, never a build failure, because npm run build gates the deploy and refusing to publish over a cosmetic tag typo would turn one missing event into a dead site update.
name: ChapterRoute

description: The teal 'Sign Up' band from the live chapter pages: a flanking-rule 'Sign Up' heading, a 'Join the Harvard in Tech Community' line, and a Subscribe pill defaulting to the shared MailChimp signup.
name: ChapterSignUp

description: Content Hub section: the org publishing channels as linked cards plus an optional latest-from-the-blog list surfaced from the blog collection.
name: ContentHub

description: Records the answer to one open runbook decision. Deliberately not just a checkbox: a step is done or it isn't, but a decision has a CONTENT, and a control that recorded only 'answered' would strand the answer in whichever meeting produced it — which is exactly why D1 has been open since 2026-07-02. The text and the flag save together, so a decision can never read as answered with nothing recorded against it, and reopening drops both. Read-only for anyone without repo write: the answer still shows, because the point of committing it is that everyone can read it.
name: DecisionTick

description: The deploy status shrunk to a line in the corner, so publishing stops interrupting the work. Shown once the full panel is dismissed, and re-attached by StagingBar on whichever admin page loads next — which is what lets an editor publish, carry on editing elsewhere, and still be told her change went live. Its colour dot is never the only signal; the label says the outcome in words.
name: DeployChip

description: The full deploy panel an editor sees after pressing Publish: a stepper from Committed through Live, the commit link, and the actions for each outcome. Dismissible at EVERY stage — it sits in a fixed full-screen scrim, so a close button that only enables on a terminal stage is a modal lock on the whole admin, which is exactly what it used to be on this site. Closing demotes it to DeployChip; the watch continues either way.
name: DeployStatus

description: External-form embed for the static site: renders one of three states — a MailChimp-style POST form (action prop), an embedded provider iframe (embedUrl prop), or an unconfigured fallback message. Delegates submission to a third-party service since a static build has no backend.
name: EmbedForm

description: Full Events page body: intro header plus Upcoming and Past sections, split from a flat events array via splitEvents. Reused by the /events route and isolated scenarios.
name: EventsPage

description: Entry-point page for /events. Loads the events content collection and renders the full Events page (Upcoming + Past) via EventsPage inside BaseLayout.
name: EventsRoute

description: Focus Areas section: crimson-edged cards for the main program categories as visual entry points, each linking into that area.
name: FocusAreas

description: Astro endpoint that emits an llms.txt AEO summary (org name, description, key pages as absolute URLs, contact email and socials) built from site settings and the env-driven site origin.
name: GET

description: Astro endpoint that emits robots.txt for whichever publishing track built it. Resolves the canonical origin from the build's configured site — falling back to the request origin — then delegates the policy itself to robotsTxtBody, passing PREVIEW_GATE_ENABLED as the disallow flag, and shapes the result as a text/plain response. The public track therefore serves allow-all plus a Sitemap line built from the real origin rather than the old static file's broken placeholder URL; the gated review track serves Disallow for everything and no Sitemap line.
name: GET

description: Giving Campaign crimson CTA band: the fundraising ask with Donate and Sponsorship actions and no fabricated progress meter.
name: GivingCampaign

description: Template React island: a name greeting with an interactive click counter. Not used on the Harvard in Tech landing page; retained from the scaffold.
name: Greeting

description: Sliding hero banner: a dark stage with a crimson scrim over rotating slides, each with a kicker, headline, serif lede, and CTA buttons; auto-advances with dot navigation via a track slider.
name: HeroCarousel

description: Harvard in Tech public home page — a faithful reproduction of harvardintech.com composed of section components (Hero, WhatsApp Community, Upcoming Events, Get Involved, Board of Directors, Support Us, Event Gallery, Contact Us), reading the events/team content collections and settings/nav singletons.
name: LandingPage

description: Events-page Luma calendar block: renders an inline iframe embed when an embed URL is set, otherwise a branded card linking out to the public Luma calendar, with a fallback when neither is set.
name: LumaCalendar

description: Landing Our Chapters section: a row of photo cards with a crimson gradient wash linking to each chapter page, sorted by order; shows a quiet prompt when empty.
name: OurChapters

description: The header's primary menu: a taxonomy mega-menu rendered to three levels — a top-level item with no children is a plain link, with children it becomes a dropdown, and if any of those children themselves have children the panel splits into titled columns. The panel opens with CSS alone via hover and focus-within, so it works before hydration and for keyboard users. It renders whatever tree it is handed and cannot tell the hand-authored groups from nav.json apart from the Chapters group the layout derives from the chapters collection, which is deliberate: derived and authored items must be indistinguishable to a visitor.
name: PrimaryNav

description: The floating pill mounted in AdminLayout, so it rides along on every admin page: it counts the browser staging set, opens the review drawer, commits every staged file as one commit, and owns the deploy watch. The watch lives in its own state beside the publish flow rather than being a phase of it, which is what allows publishing again while a deploy is still in flight.
name: StagingBar

description: Stat strip under the hero: a hairline-ruled band of big crimson figures with mono uppercase labels; values are prop-driven.
name: Stats

description: The tick control on one runbook step. Three states, and the distinction between them is the point: signed out, the box renders disabled showing whatever the branch says, because everyone can read the checklist and only repo-write holders can change it; signed in it is a real checkbox that commits; saving, the tick shows immediately while the commit is in flight with the latency stated rather than hidden, since a tick is a commit and then a rebuild. A failed commit reverts the box and says why — a tick that looks saved but was not is worse than an error, because the whole value of the page is that what it shows is what everyone else sees.
name: StepTick

description: The crimson strip above the header: a one-line where-we-are reading as a global-community lede followed by the chapter cities. The city list is derived from the chapters collection by the layout rather than hand-maintained, so it cannot fall behind the chapters the site actually has — the failure it used to have when it read the labels back out of a nav group. With no chapters it degrades to the lede alone instead of leaving a dangling separator.
name: UtilityBar

description: The alt text to render for a site-relative image URL, resolved from the media library manifest with the render site's current value as the fallback. Adopting it can never make an image's alt worse than it was: an image with no record, or a record nobody has written alt for, keeps what the component already emitted. An explicit empty string in the manifest is a real answer — 'this image is decorative' — and wins over the fallback via `??` rather than collapsing under a truthiness check, which is the distinction the whole media-manifest feature rests on.
name: altFor

description: Applies one decision answer to a progress object, returning a new one. Keeps the answer text alongside the flag so the page can show what was decided rather than only that something was — the whole reason D1 stayed open is that its answer was never written anywhere durable. Reopening drops the text with the flag, so a decision back in the open column cannot still display a conclusion it no longer holds.
name: applyDecisionAnswer

description: Applies one step toggle to a progress object, returning a new one. This is the function that decides what 'two people ticked at once' resolves to: ticks on different steps both survive, ticks on the same step converge, and an unknown id is appended rather than dropped so a step added after the file was committed is still tickable. Pure, because the caller holds an optimistic copy to revert to when the commit fails.
name: applyStepTick

description: Renders the decision ids in a step's 'Waiting on …' line as English. Replaces an inline join(' and ') that read correctly for the one and two cases the runbook has today and produced 'D1 and D2 and D3' for three — invisible because no step needs three decisions, which is exactly why it earned a function with a test. The page names what it is waiting on so the reader knows what to resolve; garbling the list undercuts the only reason it is printed.
name: blockedLabel

description: The decisions holding a runbook step up — the ones it needs that are still unanswered. Returns the ids as a list rather than a boolean because the page names them: 'waiting on D3 and D4' tells the reader what to go and resolve, where 'blocked' only tells them to give up.
name: blockingDecisions

description: Builds a mailto: URL with optional pre-filled subject/body, normalizing space encoding to %20. Used by the Support Us, Contact Us, and footer links.
name: buildMailto

description: Comparator for CMS-authored lists: ascending `order`, with entries that have no `order` sorted last rather than hoisted to the front.
name: byOrder

description: The runbook steps in one timeline bucket — beforehand, on the day, or afterwards — with order preserved. The three buckets between them must hold every step, since a step missing from the calendar is work nobody has scheduled.
name: byPhase

description: Whether this browser holds a GitHub token that could commit a runbook tick at all. Everyone can read the checklist; only repo-write holders can change it.
name: canTick

untestabilityReason.justification: A single read of the CMS package's localStorage-backed token store; there is no branching of our own to exercise.

description: Maps published chapters to header menu items — label from the chapter's own city, url built from its slug as /chapters/<slug> — ordered exactly the way the Our Chapters section orders its cards: by the order field, with city breaking ties and sorting entries that carry no order. Sharing that convention is what keeps the menu and the homepage section from ever listing the same chapters in different sequences. Callers pass chapters already draft-filtered through publishedEntries, so draft visibility stays one rule applied at every call site. Paths are returned base-agnostic; the layout wraps them in withBase at render. Returns an empty list for no chapters, and does not mutate the input.
name: chapterNavItems

description: Whether a given chip should read as pressed: exactly the selected one. Kept pure so the aria-pressed bookkeeping is testable without a DOM, and so a screen-reader user is told which filter is active rather than having to infer it from what disappeared.
name: chipPressed

description: One upload row normalized, matched, and carrying everything still undecided about it. Its ready flag means 'nothing about this row needs a human before it lands', NOT 'complete' — tier, founding and anonymous are unanswered for every row in the file no matter how clean, which is why summarizeImport reports those once for the whole import rather than as an issue on each row.
name: classifyRow

description: Dev-only Astro integration exposing a content-layer refresh endpoint the seed adapter calls after writing a scenario's markdown. Astro normally notices a seed via its file watcher, but a collection whose directory had no matching files at boot never got a watcher at all — so seeding donors or testimonials for the first time in a session changed nothing on the page. Refreshing re-runs every loader, which both ingests the new files and registers the skipped watcher. It also invalidates the data-store module and pushes a reload before answering, because Astro only invalidates rendered pages when it sees the store change on disk, and that write lands after the refresh resolves — which would leave the very next request, the capture, serving the pre-seed render.
name: codeyamContentRefresh

untestabilityReason.justification: An Astro integration hook registering Vite middleware — it exists only inside a running dev server and has no return value to assert. Its effect is what makes the seeded application scenarios render at all, so any seeded scenario capturing its data is the standing proof it works.

description: The loader every content collection uses: Astro's glob, wrapped to clear the collection's stored entries when its directory has no markdown left. Astro's own loader returns early on an empty directory, before the line that deletes the entries it did not just re-read — harmless for an always-populated collection, but every scenario re-initialises the sandbox from production before writing its seed, so a collection one scenario filled is empty for the next and the stale entries would leak across. Clearing first makes 'no files' mean 'no entries', which is what an empty directory has always meant everywhere else. The clear is scoped to the one collection being loaded.
name: collectionGlob

untestabilityReason.justification: A loader wrapper around astro/loaders glob, exercised only inside a running Astro content-layer sync. Its effect is asserted end-to-end by the scenario-isolation behaviour of momentum-fund-a-wall-of-donors and momentum-fund-arriving-from-the-email, which render different seeds on the same route without leaking into one another.

description: Re-reads the runbook's state file from the branch, applies a mutation to it, and commits the result under the editor's own GitHub identity. Read-modify-write deliberately, instead of commitAll's staged-change drift check: that check refuses the whole commit when a path moved underneath the editor, which is right for a batch of content edits reviewed as a unit and wrong for a single boolean. Refuses outright when there is no token, or when the state file is missing on the branch — inventing one would quietly commit a checklist with every step reset.
name: commitTick

untestabilityReason.justification: A GitHub REST round-trip against the live branch. The merge rule it applies is the pure applyStepTick/applyDecisionAnswer pair, both covered in cutoverTicks.test.ts; the transport is the CMS package's own commitAll.

description: Menu items for the published communities, ordered by the optional order pin and then alphabetically by name — the same rule chapterNavItems applies, so the two derivations cannot disagree about what order means. The label is the community's own name and the url is built from the slug, matching the /communities/<slug> route; building the url from the name would 404 for any community whose display name is not its slug. Callers pass entries already draft-filtered by publishedEntries.
name: communityNavItems

description: Returns the directory the content collections load from: the CODEYAM_CONTENT_ROOT sandbox during a codeyam session, else the committed src/content.
name: contentRoot

description: Returns the directory the JSON singletons (settings, nav) load from: the CODEYAM_DATA_ROOT sandbox during a codeyam session, else the committed src/data.
name: dataRoot

description: A design direction's id as every surface writes it: zero-padded to two digits. It exists because the page contradicted itself — variations.js carries num as a NUMBER, so the card badge and the full-screen bar rendered '3' while the contents list, the open questions, the README and the doc outline all said '03'. The whole purpose of the id scheme is that a reviewer writing '3' in a doc means exactly one thing, so a card labelled differently from the line they type under reintroduces the ambiguity the renumbering removed. A value that is not a number returns nothing rather than a guess, since a wrong id points a comment at the wrong design.
name: directionLabel

description: The name a supporter's node and profile card print: their real name, or the standing 'Anonymous supporter' label when they asked not to be named. Every reader-facing surface in the exploration goes through here rather than reading .name, because one component that forgets publishes a name against someone's explicit request.
name: displayName

description: The pageCopy collection entry for /donate. One page, one entry — a bare lookup shared by loadDonateUrl and loadDonateFrame so the two do not each restate the entry id, which is the kind of duplication that lets one of them keep reading a renamed entry after the other has been updated.
name: donateEntry

untestabilityReason.justification: bare astro:content getCollection lookup by entry id; every rule applied to what it returns is unit-tested in pageCopyMerge.test.ts

description: Whether a donor card stays visible under the chosen chip. Reads the tier the SERVER already resolved onto the card's data-tier, rather than re-deriving grouping in the browser, so the filtered view and the rendered view cannot disagree. The all-donors chip shows everything, which is also the state the server ships — so the page never visibly reshuffles when the script arrives.
name: donorCardVisible

description: The name to print on the wall: the standing 'Anonymous donor' label when the donor asked not to be named, otherwise their name. Every reader-facing surface goes through here rather than reading .name directly, because one component that forgets publishes a name against someone's explicit request — the single failure of a donor wall that no later edit can undo.
name: donorDisplayName

description: The outbound link a donor card renders, or none. An anonymous donor's url is suppressed even when set: a profile link beside an unnamed card identifies them exactly as surely as the name would, so anonymity that stopped at the name would be anonymity in appearance only. A blank or whitespace-only url counts as absent, since an href of a single space renders as a live link to the current page.
name: donorLinkHref

description: What a photo-less donor card draws in the avatar: the donor's initials, or a neutral dash when they are anonymous. Initials would leak the withheld name — two letters beside 'Anonymous donor' names them to anyone who knows them — so the anonymous case gets a mark that identifies nobody. Decorative either way; the card renders it aria-hidden because the name is already beside it.
name: donorMonogram

description: The headshot a donor card renders, or none. The third arm of the anonymity contract alongside donorDisplayName and donorLinkHref — a face identifies someone as surely as a name or a profile link, so an anonymous donor's photo is withheld even when the field is set. It lives beside the other two so a reader asking what anonymity actually hides finds the whole answer in one module instead of a ternary buried in a component.
name: donorPhoto

description: Returns true only for the exact string '1', so every other value — unset, empty, '0', 'false', and notably 'true' — reads as off. The shared on/off rule for the two build-time deploy flags that separate the publishing tracks: PREVIEW_GATE, read by previewGate.ts, and INCLUDE_DRAFTS, read by draftVisibility.ts, both set per track by .github/workflows/deploy.yml. Deliberately strict rather than permissive because these flags decide whether unpublished drafts reach the public site and whether the review site is gated at all, so a typo in a workflow env block must fail closed rather than have its intent guessed at. Pure and parameterised rather than reading process.env itself, so the rule is testable without faking the environment.
name: envFlagEnabled

description: The events belonging to one chapter or community, projected into the EventLike shape the event cards render. The match is an exact string comparison against the owner's collection id, because that is what /chapters/<slug> and /communities/<slug> are keyed on — a near-miss like 'New York City' for 'nyc', or a stray trailing space, belongs to nobody, which is exactly the case unmatchedChapterTags reports, so the two are two halves of one rule. An untagged event is excluded here and still appears on /events. Extracted from the two [slug].astro routes, which held this projection verbatim once communities started reusing the chapter tag.
name: eventsTaggedTo

description: Returns a new array of board members visible on the public Board of Directors, keeping every member whose active field is not explicitly false — so existing entries with no active field (and members who never toggled the CMS checkbox) remain shown. Does not mutate the input.
name: filterActiveBoardMembers

description: Formats an event date as a long en-US date string (e.g. 'September 24, 2026') for display on event cards.
name: formatEventDate

description: A volunteer project's start and end dates as one display string, or null when it has neither so the caller renders nothing rather than an empty chip. Four cases: both dates write the shared year once ("September 1 – December 15, 2026") and both years across a boundary; a start alone reads "Starts …"; an end alone reads "Through …". Each date goes through `formatEventDate`, the site's single "Month D, YYYY" formatter, so a project date and an event date cannot drift into two formats. An inverted range formats in the order authored rather than being silently swapped — a visibly wrong range gets reported, a quietly reordered one becomes a mystery — and it never throws.
name: formatProjectDates

description: The donors carrying the Founding Donor badge, in input order. Founding is recognition for giving early rather than for giving more, so it is a flag cutting across every giving level instead of a level of its own — which is what lets a founding donor keep the level that describes their actual gift.
name: foundingDonors

description: The sentence the wall prints above its bands about founding donors, or nothing when there are none. It says what the badge MEANS in words, so a first-time reader learns it once at the top rather than hovering a pill to find out. Returns nothing rather than an empty string for the zero case, which is the wall's early days when a line about a badge nobody holds would be noise.
name: foundingDonorsSummary

description: How many columns a gallery grid should use for a given photo count: one per photo up to a maximum of five, so a three-photo chapter renders three columns rather than five with two holes, while the shared 40-photo wall stays on the full-width grid. Floors at one so an empty gallery cannot produce an invalid grid-template.
name: galleryColumns

description: Pure decision for the Event Gallery fade-in: returns true when every tile should be shown immediately instead of animated — when the user prefers reduced motion, or the browser lacks IntersectionObserver (old browsers / SSR) so tiles never get stuck invisible.
name: galleryRevealImmediately

description: Returns the per-tile CSS transition-delay (ms) that staggers the Event Gallery fade-in across grid columns; tiles in the same column share a delay so each column ripples in together. Defaults to 5 columns, 60ms per column step.
name: galleryStaggerDelay

description: Whether the review track's crimson2026 passphrase overlay covers a given path. Everything is gated except the CMS preview surface — preview pages and the shareable previews index — because those exist to be handed to an outside reviewer who has no account; gating them would mean sending the link and the site passphrase together, handing that reviewer the whole unreleased site to read one page. The unguessable URL is the access mechanism instead, the same trade the repo already made for the design-review directory. A real page whose slug merely contains the word preview stays gated.
name: gateAppliesTo

description: Enumerates a route per publishable page entry for the static build, dropping any whose slug an existing route already answers for and warning about them. The routing decision itself lives in pageRouteEntries so it can be tested — getStaticPaths only runs inside a real Astro build.
name: getStaticPaths

description: Enumerates the blog collection into pre-rendered /blog/<id> routes, mapping each post entry to its slug param and props. Exercised by the blog-post-welcome route scenario.
name: getStaticPaths

description: Enumerates the chapters collection into pre-rendered /chapters/<id> routes, mapping each chapter entry to its slug param and props. Exercised by the chapter-route scenarios (the captured render proves the params resolve).
name: getStaticPaths

description: Enumerates the communities collection into pre-rendered /communities/<id> routes, mapping each community entry to its slug param and props. Draft-filtered by publishedEntries, so a drafted community is previewable under astro dev and absent from the build rather than shipping a page the menu no longer links to. Exercised by the community-route scenarios, whose captured renders prove the params resolve.
name: getStaticPaths

description: Enumerates a route per publishable page entry for the static build, dropping any whose slug an existing route already answers for and warning about them. The routing decision itself lives in pageRouteEntries so it can be tested — getStaticPaths only runs inside a real Astro build.
name: getStaticPaths

description: Enumerates the projects collection into pre-rendered /volunteer/projects/<slug> routes, mapping each project entry to its slug param and props. Draft-filtered by publishedEntries, so a project held back from the grid is readable on the review track and absent from the public build rather than staying fetchable at its own URL after being hidden. Exercised by the volunteer project detail scenarios, whose captured renders prove the params resolve.
name: getStaticPaths

description: Where to load Givebutter's widget loader from, or undefined when no account id is configured. The undefined case is the DEFAULT and the shipping state for a site that has not chosen a giving platform, so it has to mean no third-party request at all rather than an empty tag pointing at a CDN; blank and whitespace-only are treated as absent so a cleared CMS box cannot produce acct=. The id is URL-encoded because it arrives by copy-paste from Givebutter's dashboard, and a pasted value carrying & or # must not be able to add query parameters or truncate the ones already there. Pure and framework-free, the same shape as resolveGiveHref in ./giving.ts.
name: givebutterScriptSrc

description: The slugs of goal-meter sections carrying no widget id, for an advisory console.warn at build time. This state needs naming precisely because it is SILENT: a meter section with no id renders nothing at all, which is the designed behaviour and also exactly what a section an editor forgot looks like. unknownSectionKinds covers the mistyped-kind case; this covers the right-kind-wrong-field one, and the slug is what makes it diagnosable. Blank and whitespace-only count as missing, matching the component, since both render nothing. Advisory and never build-failing, the same contract its sibling carries.
name: goalMetersMissingWidgetId

description: Donors grouped into the recognition wall's bands, in the order the giving levels are declared, so the wall reads top-down from the largest commitment. Within a band the site-wide rule applies: the optional order pin first, then alphabetically by the DISPLAYED name — sorting by a withheld real name would break the alphabetical run at every anonymous card and hint at its first letter. A level with no donors is omitted rather than headed over nothing; a donor whose tier matches no declared level is not dropped but collects in a trailing 'Other supporters' group, so a renamed level or a typo costs an editor a visible mistake rather than a silently missing gift.
name: groupDonorsByTier

description: Sponsors grouped by partnership level for the /sponsor wall, in the order the levels are declared — so the wall reads top-down from the biggest commitment, matching how the levels are presented further up the page. Within a level the site-wide rule applies: the optional order pin first, then alphabetically by name. A level with no sponsors is omitted rather than rendered as a heading over nothing. A sponsor whose tier matches no declared level is NOT dropped: it collects into a trailing Other partners group, because tier is free text so the levels can be renamed in the CMS, which makes a typo possible — an editor must see their entry on the page rather than silently lose it. An untagged sponsor lands there too, the common case before anyone has picked a level.
name: groupSponsorsByLevel

description: Whether a giving-level band still has anything to show under the current filter. A band whose every card is hidden is hidden with them — otherwise the wall leaves a heading and a tier description floating over an empty row, which reads as a rendering bug rather than a filter.
name: groupVisible

description: Whether any sponsor on the wall is illustrative, which is what makes the wall render its 'example placements, not actual sponsors' notice. Deliberately ANY rather than ALL: one sample entry sitting beside three real partners is exactly the case where a reader would otherwise assume the whole row is real, so the notice has to fire on the mixed state too. Shipping sample logos silently would assert partnerships that do not exist, so this predicate is what makes shipping them honest at all.
name: hasPlaceholderSponsors

description: Chooses the campaign hero headline — the {name} template filled with a sanitized first name, or the generic headline when no usable name is present. Never leaks an unfilled {name} placeholder.
name: heroGreeting

description: The homepage anchors with no band behind them any more, so the layout can drop the menu links pointing at them. A coming-soon band is deliberately excluded: it is still on the page, so its link still lands somewhere, which is the whole difference between the two states. A band with no entry at all counts as gone, which is what a drafted band looks like after publishedEntries filters it out of a public build.
name: hiddenSectionAnchors

description: Decides whether the @codeyam/cms admin area ships in a build: only under astro dev or on the gated review track, never on the public build. The admin pages embed each entry's raw markdown in their static HTML while the CMS sign-in gate is client-side only, so wherever /admin deploys every draft's full source is publicly fetchable — putting it on the public domain would defeat the point of phasing content. Dev keeps it so the codeyam Live Preview retains its admin scenarios. Extracted from astro.config.mjs because that file can only be exercised by a real astro build and cannot be imported under vitest.
name: includeCmsIntegration

description: Whether the domain cutover runbook route is built at all. Dev and the gated review track only — the same answer /admin gets. Decided at build time rather than left to PreviewGate because the gate un-gates on the public track by design, so without this the cutover would have published the page naming where the domain's records live on the public domain, ungated. This is the runbook's own decision D4 settled in code.
name: includeCutoverRunbook

description: Decides whether a build publishes a sitemap: the public track only. The review origin is noindex and serves Disallow for everything, so it has nothing to offer a sitemap and emitting one would contradict the gate. Must stay in agreement with robotsTxtBody, which omits its Sitemap line on the same track — if the two disagree the review site advertises a sitemap URL that 404s. Extracted from astro.config.mjs alongside includeCmsIntegration so the decision is unit-testable.
name: includeSitemapIntegration

description: Dev-only helper that (re)creates the .codeyam/tmp/content-sandbox copy of src/content and src/data, so the codeyam dev server reads/seeds the sandbox and never the committed production markdown.
name: initContentSandbox

untestabilityReason.justification: filesystem boundary — rmSync/cpSync of content/data dirs; no branching logic to unit-test

description: Idempotent DOM wiring for the wall's tier chips, in the initGalleryReveal mould: no-ops under SSR, when the wall is absent, and when it renders no chips. Every donor's name is already in the static HTML under a real heading, so this script only HIDES — with JavaScript off the wall is the same complete list it always was. Cards are hidden with the hidden attribute rather than a class so a filtered-out donor leaves the accessibility tree too.
name: initDonorFilter

description: Idempotent, SSR-safe DOM wiring for the Event Gallery fade-in: reveals every tile immediately when galleryRevealImmediately says to, otherwise observes each tile via IntersectionObserver and adds the in-view class as it scrolls into the viewport, unobserving once revealed.
name: initGalleryReveal

description: Idempotent, SSR-safe DOM wiring for click-to-enlarge: binds each gallery tile to open its photo in the native `dialog`, plus the close/prev/next controls and the backdrop click. No-ops without a DOM or `HTMLDialogElement`, which is what leaves the un-enhanced gallery usable rather than half-bound. Resolves the tile list at click time rather than capturing it, so tiles bound before 'Show all' still arrow through the photos it reveals, and skips tiles inside a hidden `.gallery-item` so arrowing never lands on a photo that is not in the grid.
name: initLightbox

description: Idempotent client-side DOM wiring for the banner parallax: no-op under SSR/vitest and on re-invocation. When parallaxEnabled (read via matchMedia) is true, sizes every [data-parallax] to 100vh and, on a rAF-throttled scroll/resize listener, sets translateY(parallaxOffset(rootTop)) so the photo stays fixed while its [data-parallax-root] section scrolls over it; otherwise leaves the images as static object-fit: cover. Hoisted from Hero.astro and GetInvolved.astro.
name: initParallax

description: Derives up-to-two-letter uppercase initials from a board member name, used as the BoardMemberCard avatar fallback when a member has no photo.
name: initials

description: Walks the menu tree to its full three levels and collects every site-internal url in declaration order — internal meaning rooted at a slash. External links out to Medium, LinkedIn, and the newsletter are skipped, since they point at another site and have no local page to resolve against. Feeds the nav integrity guard together with unresolvedNavUrls.
name: internalNavUrls

description: Whether a runbook decision is recorded answered in the progress singleton. Same tolerance for an absent entry as isStepDone, and the same reason: the state file is hand-editable.
name: isDecisionAnswered

description: Whether a preview is password-protected, meaning its title and body are encrypted at rest and the stored body is base64 ciphertext rather than markdown. BlogPostBody branches on this: rendering a locked entry through the ordinary markdown path shows the reader a wall of base64, which is exactly what happened on the first attempt at the feature.
name: isLocked

description: Whether an entry is an unlisted preview page. previewOf is the only marker — a slug that merely looks like a preview does not count. Routes pass this to SEO's noindex prop so a preview leaked to the public track stays out of search results, which the review track's passphrase gate cannot do because that gate is off on the public build.
name: isPreview

description: Whether one slug is safe to publish at the site root — the single-slug form of shadowedPageSlugs, for a caller checking as it goes.
name: isReservedPageSlug

description: Whether a supporter can be found by typing their name in the network's search box. False for anyone who asked not to be named. The live donor wall already withholds an anonymous donor's name, photo, link and initials together, and a search box is a new way to undo all four at once — so anonymity has to reach it. They remain a visible node counting toward every total and every milestone, because withholding the node instead would make the wall quietly undercount people who asked only not to be named.
name: isSearchable

description: Whether a runbook step is recorded done in the progress singleton. A step absent from the file reads as not done rather than throwing — the file is committed and hand-editable, so an entry predating a step is reachable rather than theoretical.
name: isStepDone

description: Whether a cutover step can be started right now: every decision it needs is answered and it is not already done. Excluding done steps is what keeps the banner's 'could be started today' count from counting finished work.
name: isStepReady

description: Maps a KeyboardEvent.key to a lightbox action — Escape to close, the arrows to next/prev — or null to ignore it. Mapping Escape is deliberate redundancy: `dialog` closes itself on Escape, so routing it here keeps ONE close path that also runs our teardown rather than letting the native cancel and our handler drift apart.
name: lightboxKeyAction

description: Reads the accomplishments collection into the card shape MomentumAccomplishments already took from copy.accomplishments. Migrated out of donatePage.json, a singleton the CMS does not model at all, which is what made these cards developer-only. Maps the schema's description key onto the component's body prop because body is a reserved field id in the CMS registry and a custom field claiming it is dropped from the editor without comment.
name: loadAccomplishments

description: Loads the committed or seeded tick state for the cutover runbook from the cutoverProgress.json singleton. Read through readSingleton so it honours the codeyam sandbox redirect, which is what lets each scenario seed a different state without touching production.
name: loadCutoverProgress

untestabilityReason.justification: A filesystem read of a singleton path; the parsing and sandbox-resolution it delegates to are covered by contentRoot.test.ts, and the shapes it returns are exercised throughout cutoverProgress.test.ts.

description: Reads the pageCopy entry for /donate and returns the campaign page's frame fields merged over donatePage.json, for the route to spread onto the copy object alongside the accomplishments, pillars and donation URL the sibling loaders supply.
name: loadDonateFrame

untestabilityReason.justification: astro:content getCollection boundary; the merge rules it delegates to are unit-tested in pageCopyMerge.test.ts

description: Where every giving button points, read from the pageCopy entry for the donate page with the donatePage.json value as fallback. This is the field that had to become editable before the migration: resolveGiveHref was already written to switch every Give button the moment a platform URL exists, so the only thing missing was somewhere an editor could type it. Blank anywhere keeps all of them on the giving-inquiry mailto, which is the production state today.
name: loadDonateUrl

description: Reads the donors collection and reshapes it into the plain records every rule in lib/donors.ts takes. The thin untestable edge split off from the pure module, exactly as momentumSectionsContent.ts is split from momentumSections.ts, and a module rather than page frontmatter because the isolated-component harness needs the identical pipeline. Drafts follow the site-wide rule so an entry stays hidden until the gift clears; production returns nothing today, where the wall renders its invitation state.
name: loadDonors

description: Reads the heroSlides collection and returns the published slides in editor order. The slides were HeroCarousel prop defaults, which were the live content because index.astro rendered the carousel with no props, so the most prominent copy on the site was the one thing no editor could reach. An empty result is meaningful rather than an error: the carousel falls back to its own defaults, so the top of the site cannot render blank because someone drafted every slide.
name: loadHeroSlides

description: Reads the homeSections collection and returns the published bands in editor order plus any unrecognized kinds for the caller to warn about. The thin astro:content edge kept out of the pure rules module, and a module rather than page frontmatter because TWO callers need the identical list: index.astro renders the bands and BaseLayout reads them to prune menu links to hidden ones. A second hand-rolled copy would drift, and the two disagreeing is exactly the menu-points-at-a-missing-band failure the visibility rule exists to prevent.
name: loadHomeSections

description: Reads the stats collection and returns the published figures in editor order. Migrated off homeStats in settings.json, which held the real numbers but had no input in the CMS because the package renders five scalar settings fields and round-trips every other key untouched, so the figures were editable data nobody could edit. Empty falls back to the component defaults the same way the hero does.
name: loadHomeStats

description: Reads the single siteIntegrations entry and merges the analytics id, the Givebutter account id, and the custom head/body HTML over settings.json. Called from components rather than routes — Analytics, GivebutterWidgets, HeadExtras, and the two shells that inject body HTML — because these belong to every page, and threading them through every route's props would be the one arrangement where a new shell could silently ship without analytics or without the widgets loader.
name: loadIntegrations

untestabilityReason.justification: astro:content getCollection boundary; the merge rules it delegates to are unit-tested in pageCopyMerge.test.ts

description: Reads the momentumSections collection and returns the published sections in editor order plus any unrecognized kinds for the caller to warn about, rendering each narrative entry's markdown body. The thin astro:content edge kept out of the pure rules module, and shared by the /donate route and the isolated-component harness so the pipeline exists once.
name: loadMomentumSections

description: Reads the pillars collection into the card shape GiftPillars already took from copy.pillars, passing each icon through resolvePillarIcon so whatever an editor typed becomes one of the three drawn glyphs. Migrated out of donatePage.json for the same reason the accomplishment cards were, and renames description to body for the same reserved-field-id reason.
name: loadPillars

description: Reads the single sponsorPage entry and its levels concurrently and merges both over the committed sponsorPage.json, so /sponsor renders from content an editor controls while the JSON remains the fallback.
name: loadSponsorCopy

untestabilityReason.justification: astro:content getCollection boundary; the merge rules it delegates to are unit-tested in pageCopyMerge.test.ts

description: Fetches the published sponsorLevels entries and hands them to sponsorLevelsFrom. A bare boundary call: the ordering and the empty-means-null rule deliberately live in the pure helper so they are exercised by unit tests rather than only by a rendered page.
name: loadSponsorLevels

untestabilityReason.justification: bare astro:content getCollection passthrough; all ordering and null-vs-empty logic is unit-tested in sponsorLevelsFrom via pageCopyMerge.test.ts

description: Reads the single volunteerPage collection entry and merges it over the committed JSON. The thin astro:content edge kept out of the pure rules module, the same split momentumSectionsContent and donatePageContent already use. It exists because this copy used to live only in volunteerPage.json, a singleton the CMS models no editor for, so rewriting the volunteer pitch was a developer's job.
name: loadVolunteerCopy

untestabilityReason.justification: astro:content getCollection boundary; the merge rules it delegates to are unit-tested in pageCopyMerge.test.ts

description: Whether the name column is really an anonymity request. The upload has no anonymity column, so a supporter asking not to be named has only the free text field to say it in — 'Anonymous', 'Withheld', 'Prefer not to say'. Imported literally the wall shows a card reading 'Anonymous' as though that were somebody's name. Matches the whole normalized cell rather than a substring, so a real name that merely contains a marker word keeps its identity.
name: looksAnonymous

description: One row of the bi-weekly supporter spreadsheet, re-keyed from its human column headings onto the field names every import rule reads. The seam worth having a function for: the rules read row.gradYear while the file says 'Class Year', so a renamed heading yields undefined for every row — normalizeGradYear then returns null fourteen times and the import reports 'no usable class year' for the whole file while looking like it worked. A column the donors collection has nowhere to put is dropped rather than carried, since carrying it would imply the wall can show it; a heading the file omits stays absent rather than becoming an empty string, because 'not supplied' and 'supplied blank' are different answers downstream.
name: mapUploadRow

description: Every row of an upload, mapped through mapUploadRow. Returns an empty list rather than throwing when handed a file that failed to parse, because this runs on a published review page where an exception costs the reviewer the whole walkthrough rather than one row.
name: mapUploadRows

description: How one spreadsheet row relates to the supporters already on the wall: new, duplicate, or possible. The middle outcome is the point — names differing only by punctuation or a suffix might be one person or might be relatives, and deciding automatically either duplicates someone or merges two people, so it does neither and asks. A duplicate whose existing record is anonymous is flagged separately, because that is the specific path by which a withheld name reaches the public site: the upload carries the real name and no anonymity column, so a blind overwrite republishes what someone asked to keep private.
name: matchExisting

description: Whether a donor belongs under a given giving-level id — the predicate behind the filter chips, shared by the server render and the client script on purpose. Two copies of 'which tier is this donor in?' is two answers that can disagree, and the one a visitor sees would be the client's. The trailing-group id matches exactly the donors groupDonorsByTier files there: untagged, or tagged with a level the page does not declare.
name: matchesTier

description: The Momentum Fund page's fixed frame — the hero above the reorderable sections and the closing ask below them — over the committed donatePage.json. Returns ONLY the frame keys so the route can spread it over the copy object without clobbering the fields loadAccomplishments, loadPillars and loadDonateUrl own. The frame becomes editable copy and deliberately stays out of the momentumSections collection: a page whose hero could be dragged to the bottom is a page an editor can break, and making the wording changeable does not make the position changeable. The personalized headline carries the name placeholder the browser fills from the campaign link, so a cleared one falling back is what protects the email campaign's whole premise.
name: mergeDonateFrame

description: The site-wide integration keys over settings.json: the analytics id, the Givebutter account id, and the custom head/body HTML. The fallback matters more here than anywhere else in this migration. Every other field degrades to slightly stale copy, while these degrade to a site with no analytics and no verification tags, or to every goal meter silently failing to render, on every page, with nothing visible to notice. So a deleted entry or a cleared box falls back to the committed settings rather than to off, and turning either integration off is consequently a two-step edit, the right trade against one mistake silently unhooking measurement or the meter from the whole site.
name: mergeIntegrations

description: The /sponsor copy over the committed sponsorPage.json, with the partnership levels re-attached so groupSponsorsByLevel and every child component keep the exact input they always took. Levels arrive as null rather than an empty array when nothing has been migrated, which is what keeps 'an editor deleted every level' distinguishable from 'this collection is empty' — falling back on the first would resurrect levels someone deliberately removed. The inquiry form URL deliberately does NOT fall back: blank is the production state and renders the unconfigured placeholder, so falling back would make taking a form back down impossible once one had been set.
name: mergeSponsorCopy

description: The /volunteer copy an editor's content entry produces over the committed volunteerPage.json. Field-by-field via preferText, because the CMS has no notion of a required singleton: an editor can delete the only entry or clear one field, and both are ordinary mistakes that must cost a stale line of copy rather than a blank hero. The benefits list is the exception and is ALL-OR-NOTHING: an editor part-way through rewriting the blocks means the list they are building, so a half-finished list is never topped up from the JSON, and an emptied list is honoured because removing the band is itself a real edit.
name: mergeVolunteerCopy

description: The milestone the supporter count passed between two frames of the growth animation, or null. Crossing rather than landing: the growth step accelerates as the count climbs, so asking whether the new count EQUALS a milestone means 50, 100 and 150 fire only when the arithmetic happens to hit them exactly — which in practice never happened, and 200 only appeared to work because it is clamped. When one step clears several, the earliest wins so no moment the campaign wants to mark is skipped.
name: milestoneCrossed

description: Pulls the `name` parameter out of a full URL or a bare query string, returning null when absent or unparseable.
name: nameFromSearch

description: The gallery index `delta` steps from `current`, wrapping at both ends. Wraps rather than clamps because a lightbox is a carousel, not a list: arrowing past the last photo should reach the first, and a disabled arrow at each end is a dead control the user has to notice. Returns 0 for an empty gallery so a caller cannot index into nothing, and normalizes the negative modulo that a naive expression would produce going backwards off the front.
name: nextPhotoIndex

description: A four-digit graduation year from a spreadsheet cell, or nothing. Accepts the apostrophe form people actually write and a spreadsheet preserves as text, reading two digits as 1930-2029 — a Harvard alum's class year is neither 2104 nor 1904. Returns nothing rather than a guess for anything else, because a wrong year is worse than a missing one here: it places a supporter in the wrong cohort in three of the nine directions, where the error looks exactly like data.
name: normalizeGradYear

description: A supporter's name reduced to the form two spellings of one person share: trimmed, inner whitespace collapsed, diacritics stripped, lowercased. Each of those is a real way one human arrives twice — a padded cell from a spreadsheet export, 'Tomas' for 'Tomás', an uppercasing web form — and a bare equality check misses all of them, putting a second card on the wall for someone already there. Punctuation is deliberately KEPT so a suffix does not silently merge two people: 'Gregory Tanaka-Lindqvist III' may be the same person as 'Gregory Tanaka Lindqvist' or may be his father, and collapsing them deletes a supporter without telling anyone. That case is surfaced as a possible match for a human instead.
name: normalizeName

description: The site's spelling of a Harvard school, from whatever the spreadsheet says. Someone filling a form writes it out in full while the site stores a short form, so without the alias map an ordinary correct answer arrives as an unknown value. An unrecognized school passes through unchanged rather than being discarded — it is a mapping to confirm, not a value to drop, and losing it silently would empty that supporter out of the three directions that group by school. An empty cell returns nothing rather than an empty school, since 'the file did not say' is what rowIssues reports on.
name: normalizeSchool

description: Normalize a slug for comparison — trimmed, lowercased, and stripped of surrounding slashes. Exists because a CMS slug box accepts all three variations, so an editor typing /About/ has made the same collision as one typing about, and a raw string compare would miss it.
name: normalizeSlug

description: Selects the volunteer projects to render — those not explicitly closed (`active !== false`), ordered by `order`. Absent `active` means open, matching the board-member convention, so a project whose toggle was never touched still shows.
name: openProjects

description: The homepage bands in the order an editor arranged them, with any band whose kind matches no component dropped. The homepage counterpart to orderedSections: sorted by the optional Order pin via sortByOrder so an unnumbered band sorts last instead of jumping to the top, and coming-soon and hidden bands are kept in the list because classification is the caller's job.
name: orderedHomeSections

description: The Momentum Fund page sections in the order an editor arranged them: sorted by the optional Order pin via the site-wide sortByOrder, with any section whose kind matches no renderer dropped rather than rendered blank. Callers pass entries already draft-filtered by publishedEntries.
name: orderedSections

description: Splits page entries into the ones that get a route and the ones dropped for colliding with an existing address, returning both plus the warning. Extracted from getStaticPaths, where the shadow list was computed twice and nothing could be tested because getStaticPaths only runs inside a real Astro build.
name: pageRouteEntries

description: Resolves a page's title, description, and share image: the explicit SEO override, else the page's own visible copy. Treats a blank-but-present override as absent — the CMS writes an empty string when an editor clears the box, and a bare nullish-coalesce would have published a page with no title at all.
name: pageSeo

description: The Astro base a GitHub Pages project site must be built with: the repo name rooted with a leading slash, because such a site is served from <user>.github.io/<repo>/. Exists so the deploy workflow's DEPLOY_BASE_PATH can be checked against the repo it actually publishes to rather than being two hand-matched strings sitting far apart in the YAML. Throws on an empty repo name instead of returning a bare slash: a bare slash is the base of a user site or a custom domain, so returning it would turn a missing value into a plausible-looking one that builds every asset URL wrong.
name: pagesBasePathFor

description: Pure gate deciding whether the scroll parallax runs: returns fineHover && !reducedMotion. Encodes the desktop-only / prefers-reduced-motion policy (parallax is janky or ignored on touch browsers) as testable logic, separate from the matchMedia DOM reads in initParallax.
name: parallaxEnabled

description: Pure helper returning the translateY (px) that keeps a banner pinned to the viewport top as its section scrolls: returns -sectionTop, where sectionTop is the section's getBoundingClientRect().top. Reproduces the background-attachment: fixed look on the Hero and Get Involved banners without CSS background-image (which the preview proxy / Pages base path rewrite breaks).
name: parallaxOffset

description: Whether a typed passphrase opens one of the review artifacts. Surrounding whitespace is forgiven because the passphrase is shared out of band and arrives pasted out of an email, carrying a trailing space more often than not; case is not, since a case-insensitive passphrase is a materially weaker one and case is not a likely error when pasting. The case worth having a function for at all: an empty expected passphrase never opens the gate. Trimming an empty string still equals an empty string, so the bare comparison this replaced would have admitted anyone who merely clicked the button had the build ever substituted a blank value. build.py refuses to emit one; this is the same guard at the point the decision is actually made, because a published page outlives the build that produced it. Plain JavaScript with a UMD wrapper for the same reason donorNetwork.js is: build.py inlines it verbatim into a self-contained page that must work from a file:// open and under a CSP blocking every host, while vitest imports it as CommonJS. Distinct from previewGate.ts, which is server-only, decides whether the whole site build is gated, and un-gates on the public track by design; it stays the source of the passphrase value, which build.py parses out of it.
name: passphraseAccepted

description: The editor's value for a copy field if it holds anything, otherwise the value committed in JSON. Whitespace-only counts as empty, because a field an editor cleared usually still holds the newline the textarea left behind and treating that as real copy puts a blank heading on the live page. The returned value is trimmed. The deliberate consequence is that a field cannot be blanked from the CMS while the JSON still carries a value: emptying a heading is a two-step edit, which is the right trade when the opposite choice's failure mode is a live page with a missing headline.
name: preferText

description: Projects collection entries projected into the flat shape the cards render, with the entry's `id` promoted to `slug`. Lives in the lib rather than inline in the detail route because it is the piece most likely to drift silently: a new field on the `projects` schema that is not added here simply never reaches a suggestion card, with no type error and no failing build to say so. Keeps `relatedProjects` and every card component free of any `astro:content` type. Non-mutating; preserves input order so the caller decides sorting.
name: projectCardData

description: Which sign-up call-to-action a project's detail page offers, or null for none. The project's own `applyUrl` wins; with none it falls back to the site-wide volunteer CTA, because a project posted before its sign-up form exists still needs a way in and a page that simply ends after the description leaves a willing reader nowhere to go. Only when neither link exists does the page render no ask, rather than a dead button. Empty strings count as absent, not as links, so an editor who cleared the field cannot produce an href pointing at the current page.
name: projectCta

description: The URL of one volunteer project's detail page, `/volunteer/projects/<slug>`. The route file and every card that links to it derive their URL from this one place, so the two cannot drift apart — a card pointing at a path the route does not generate is exactly the 404 this helper exists to prevent. Site-root-relative on purpose: callers wrap it in `withBase` so it resolves under both deploy bases, and applying the base here would double the prefix.
name: projectPath

description: Returns a new array of the content-collection entries fit to publish, keeping every entry whose draft flag is not explicitly true — so an absent flag, which is the state of every existing entry and what the CMS writes when the Draft toggle is off, means live, and a hand-written draft false is treated the same as absent. Pass includeDrafts to keep drafts in the list; every call site takes it from the shared INCLUDE_DRAFTS constant in draftVisibility.ts, so drafts stay visible under astro dev for author preview and on the review track, and are omitted from the public build. The flag is an explicit parameter rather than an internal env read so both halves of the rule are testable without faking the environment. Does not mutate the input.
name: publishedEntries

description: The repository name parsed out of a git remote URL, accepting the SSH form the deploy job uses and the HTTPS form, with or without the .git suffix. Takes a whole command line rather than a bare URL so the deploy-workflow contract test can hand it a run block directly, keeping the parsing rule next to its own tests instead of inside a test file. Returns undefined rather than throwing when there is no remote, because a step that pushes nowhere is a real state: the reviewed track publishes by artifact upload and has no remote at all.
name: pushTargetRepo

description: Reads the CMS media library manifest from `<dataRoot>/media.json` — the singleton the package writes from /admin — returning an empty library when the file is absent or malformed, so production before the first upload and any scenario that seeds no media still render rather than failing the build. Goes through `dataRoot()` like the settings and nav singletons so a codeyam session's sandbox redirect reaches it and the seed adapter can seed a `media` key per scenario.
name: readMediaManifest

description: Reads and JSON-parses one singleton data file from the resolved dataRoot(), so every singleton read honours the codeyam sandbox redirect. Moved here from site.ts and de-duplicated when cutoverProgress.ts grew a second identical private copy - two implementations of respecting the sandbox is how one of them ends up not respecting it. Server-only: it touches the filesystem at call time.
name: readSingleton

untestabilityReason.justification: filesystem boundary — readFileSync + JSON.parse of a data-dir file

description: Up to `limit` other open projects to suggest at the bottom of one project's detail page. "Related" means ADJACENT IN EDITOR ORDER, wrapping past the end — not semantically similar: the collection carries no tag, category, or topic field, so there is nothing to compute similarity from, and of the honest alternatives the editor's own ordering is the only one reflecting a human decision. Wrapping means the last project still gets suggestions instead of none. Filtered through `openProjects` so a retired project is never advertised at the bottom of an open one — the detail route generates a page for every published entry regardless of `active`. Returns an empty list when there is no other open project, which is the collection's real state today.
name: relatedProjects

description: Resolves where a giving CTA points: the donation platform when `donateUrl` is configured, otherwise a mailto with a campaign-specific subject. Treats empty/whitespace-only as unset and trims pasted URLs, so a cleared CMS field cannot produce href="".
name: resolveGiveHref

description: Decides whether a build renders entries flagged draft, from whether it is a production build and the raw INCLUDE_DRAFTS env value. Drafts show when the build is not a production build — astro dev, and therefore the codeyam preview and every scenario capture — or when the build explicitly opts in with INCLUDE_DRAFTS=1, which is the review track. This exists because both publishing tracks are production builds: the review site at review.harvardintech.com is not astro dev, so the bare import.meta.env.PROD inference that every publishedEntries call site used to inline cannot express it. The opt-in is checked through envFlagEnabled so a misspelled value leaves the public default of hiding drafts.
name: resolveIncludeDrafts

description: Normalizes a narrative section's free-text layout field to image-left, image-right, or text-only, trimming and lowercasing first. Anything unrecognized becomes text-only, the one layout that reads correctly with or without a photo, so a mistyped value degrades to readable prose instead of an empty column.
name: resolveLayout

description: Normalizes a gift-pillar icon value to one of the three glyphs PillarIcon actually draws, falling back to people for a typo, a blank, or an absent key. The boundary that lets icon be free text: the CMS has no select control, so an editor types the value, and a mistake must cost them the icon they wanted rather than the build. Mirrors resolveLayout in momentumSections.ts.
name: resolvePillarIcon

description: Turns a section's two toggles into one of three states: shown, coming-soon, or hidden. Two booleans rather than a three-valued field because the CMS field types stop at text/number/textarea/date/image/boolean/list, so a tri-state would be free text an editor has to type exactly right. Draft wins over comingSoon, so a band an editor hid can never also advertise itself. Shared by the homepage and the Momentum Fund page so both phase a section by the same rule.
name: resolveVisibility

description: The outline a reviewer pastes into a doc, built from the LIVE directions list the deck renders its cards from rather than a transcription of it. The review page collects nothing on purpose — a published artifact cannot post anywhere, and a review needing a backend stops working when the link outlives the server — so the outline is the actual interface between the page and the reviewer's notes, and it must name every id the page shows. Hand-written beside the page it would fail that silently: rename a direction and the outline keeps the old name, so the reviewer types under headings that no longer match what they are looking at, and the drift lands in their feedback instead of in a build. The off-brief pair is labelled as controls so they are not read as two more candidates, and no line carries trailing whitespace, which would survive the paste as invisible junk.
name: reviewOutline

description: A seeded pseudo-random generator (mulberry32) giving each direction a reproducible layout. Determinism is the point: a network that reshuffles between renders reads as a different design, so a reviewer would be rating noise — and a screenshot they already commented on would stop matching the page.
name: rng

description: Builds a robots.txt body for either publishing track, taking the resolved sitemap URL and a disallowAll flag. The public track gets allow-all directives plus the Sitemap reference; the gated review track gets Disallow for everything and, deliberately, no Sitemap line at all, because astro.config.mjs omits the sitemap integration on that track so advertising sitemap-index.xml there would point crawlers at a 404. Extracted out of the robots.txt endpoint and given the gate as a parameter so both tracks' output is unit-testable — the endpoint resolves the gate from process.env at module load, so a test importing it could only ever reach one branch. The endpoint keeps origin resolution and response shaping.
name: robotsTxtBody

description: The counts the runbook's standing banner prints: steps done, decisions answered, how many are ready versus blocked, plus the complete and untouched flags that select which of the three banners renders. Totals come from the authored runbook rather than the state file, so a state file missing entries cannot shrink the denominator shown to the team.
name: rollup

description: The entries a collection's getStaticPaths should BUILD: everything publishedEntries returns, plus every preview page. The deliberate mirror image of the listing rule — a preview is kept out of every index so nothing links to it, but its page must still be generated or the token URL handed to a reviewer 404s. A preview stays routable even when it also carries draft:true, since hiding it from the site was never the point. Keeps the positional includeDrafts signature the fifteen existing call sites use rather than the package's options-object form, which would silently degrade to the package's own environment guess and break the two-track draft rule.
name: routableEntries

description: Everything wrong with, or undecidable about, one upload row, each carrying a severity. Blocking means the row cannot become a supporter without a human — no name at all, an anonymity request sitting in the name column, or a re-import that would unmask someone already anonymous. Review means it can land but a decision was deferred, which is where an ordinary duplicate and a missing school or class year sit. Nothing is auto-corrected: that is the contract, because each wrong guess costs a misstated giving level, an unearned badge, or a published name, and only the last is beyond repair by a later edit.
name: rowIssues

description: Normalizes a raw ?name= value into a display-safe first name, or null when it is absent, over-long, or does not look like a name. The security boundary for the /donate hero: the value is attacker-controlled via URL, so markup and digits are rejected and only the first token is kept.
name: sanitizeFirstName

description: The element id a band's coming-soon placeholder must carry so a menu link still lands on it, derived from that band's entry in HOME_SECTION_ANCHORS. Derived rather than a second table because the anchor and the id are the same fact written two ways, and a hand-maintained copy would eventually disagree and leave a placeholder unreachable from the menu still linking to it.
name: sectionAnchorId

description: The page slugs something else already answers for, in input order. Returns the offending slugs rather than a boolean so the build warning can name them, and compares case- and slash-insensitively because a slug box accepts both.
name: shadowedPageSlugs

description: The build-time warning naming the shadowed slugs and where to rename them, or null when nothing was dropped. Advisory rather than fatal, matching the orphan-chapter-tag warning: refusing to build over one badly-slugged page would turn a single invisible page into a dead site update.
name: shadowedSlugWarning

description: Formats an ISO timestamp as a short '8 Aug' for the attribution line beside a GitHub login on the cutover runbook. Day and month only — every tick happens inside one migration window, so a year costs width and tells the reader nothing. An unparseable value yields an empty string rather than 'Invalid Date', because the timestamps live in a committed, hand-editable JSON file and a mangled one should cost a missing date, not a broken-looking page.
name: shortDate

description: The short label for a Harvard school — HBS, SEAS, College — used wherever the full name will not fit. An unrecognized school passes through unchanged rather than becoming blank, so a typo in the bi-weekly upload costs a long label rather than silently losing the supporter's affiliation.
name: shortSchool

description: Whether the wall is worth putting filter chips on. One band means the chips would read 'All donors / Leadership Circle' over a list already on screen — a control that filters nothing, which is worse than no control. Chips earn their place only once there is somewhere else to go.
name: shouldShowTierChips

description: Loads the editable settings/nav singletons from the resolved data root (sandbox-aware) via readSingleton: fs read + JSON.parse.
name: site

description: Maps a social link icon field (twitter/facebook/email, case-insensitive) to its self-hosted asset path under public/images/social/. Returns null for unknown or missing icons so the Contact Us section degrades to a label-only link. Icons were downloaded from the original harvardintech.com site to keep the GitHub Pages build CDN-independent.
name: socialIconSrc

description: Returns a new array of board members ordered by ascending order field (missing order treated as 0), so the public Board of Directors matches the curated sequence regardless of on-disk file order.
name: sortBoardMembers

description: Non-mutating sort by `order`, shared by the volunteer-projects and testimonials lists.
name: sortByOrder

description: Splits a flat event list into upcoming (date >= now, soonest first) and past (date < now, most recent first) relative to a reference time; events at now count as upcoming.
name: splitEvents

description: Splits a board member's role into display lines on a '·' separator (e.g. "Founder · Harvard C'08" -> ["Founder", "Harvard C'08"]), trimming surrounding whitespace; a role without a separator returns a single-element array. Used by BoardMemberCard to render the role over two lines.
name: splitRole

description: The partnership levels a set of collection entries produces: ordered by the editor's order pin, reshaped for the page, or null when there are none. The null return is the whole reason this exists apart from toSponsorLevels — it is the signal mergeSponsorCopy needs to tell 'an editor deleted every level' apart from 'nothing has been migrated into this collection yet'. The second must fall back to the committed JSON and the first must not, or removing a level would silently undo itself on the next build. Takes the entries rather than their data so the loader above it stays a bare fetch with no reshaping of its own.
name: sponsorLevelsFrom

description: The whole upload classified, plus the fields it structurally cannot fill. The unresolvable and unmodelled lists come back unconditionally rather than only when something goes wrong, because they are properties of the FILE FORMAT and not of any row: a spreadsheet where every line is spotless still cannot say who gave at what level, who is a founding donor, or who asked to stay anonymous, and it still carries school and class year the donors collection has no field for. A summary that hid them on a clean file would report success for a job it did a third of.
name: summarizeImport

description: The sentence under the progress count in the runbook's partway banner. Pure so the pluralisation is testable — it was a nested ternary in markup, where '1 steps are waiting' is the kind of thing that ships because nobody seeds exactly one blocked step while looking at the page. The two branches say different things deliberately: with something blocked the useful fact is what is stuck; with nothing blocked it is that the decisions are all in.
name: summaryLine

description: The mark drawn in a supporter's avatar on the network explorations: their initials, or a neutral dash when they asked not to be named. Named for what it produces rather than reusing 'initials' from team.ts, which takes a name string and knows nothing about anonymity — this one takes the whole supporter because the anonymous case must return a mark identifying nobody. Initials would leak the withheld name, since two letters beside 'Anonymous supporter' identifies them to anyone who knows them. Capped at two letters so a long name cannot spell itself out.
name: supporterMonogram

description: N items spread evenly across a larger list, used to place supporters through points sampled from a letterform. Taking the first N instead would fill the top of the first glyph and leave the rest of the word empty, because the sampler emits points in scan order. Returns a copy, so a caller cannot mutate the sampled source.
name: thin

description: The commit subject a runbook tick lands under, so the repo history reads as migration progress rather than a series of 'Update cutoverProgress.json'. Distinguishes completing from reopening, since those are different events.
name: tickCommitMessage

description: One boolean per section saying whether it renders on the tinted band. Narrative sections alternate tinted and untinted so consecutive prose stays separated; the counter advances only on narratives, so a bespoke band between two of them does not flip the rhythm. Pure, replacing a counter that was mutated inside the page's render map.
name: tintedFlags

description: Coerces a string-or-Date event date into a Date, passing existing Date instances through untouched.
name: toEventDate

description: Normalizes a gallery's photos to a single shape from either call form: the landing page's plain srcs or the CMS's `{ image, caption? }` rows. Drops rows whose image is missing or blank — the CMS list control adds an empty row before a photo is picked, and rendering it would give a tile with no image and a lightbox that opens onto nothing — and treats a whitespace-only caption as absent so no empty figcaption takes space under the photo.
name: toGalleryPhotos

description: Reduces a nav url to the page it actually lands on, so the integrity guard compares like with like: any fragment is dropped so an anchor link resolves against its own page, a bare hash resolves against the home page, and a trailing slash is ignored. Module-private to nav.ts and exercised through unresolvedNavUrls, whose tests pin each of those three normalizations.
name: toPath

description: Partnership levels reshaped from their collection entries into the shape every /sponsor component already consumes. Two storage quirks meet here. Each level s benefits are stored as rows of a single text field rather than as bare strings, because the CMS s repeatable list is a list of field rows and offers no plain-string list control — the same constraint that forced levels out of sponsorPage.json into their own collection, since a list inside a list is not expressible at all.
