And the level KEY that a sponsor s tier matches on comes from the entry itself (its filename), never from frontmatter: an editable id text box would silently re-home every sponsor filed under the level when retyped, and the seed adapter strips id as a filename key, which made the collection unseedable while such a field existed.
name: toSponsorLevels

description: The unrecognized kind values on the homepage, de-duplicated and in first-seen order, for an advisory build-time warning. Advisory rather than build-failing for the same reason unknownSectionKinds is: kind is free text because the CMS has no select control, so a typo must cost that editor one band and a log line, never the deploy.
name: unknownHomeSectionKinds

description: The unrecognized kind values in a section list, de-duplicated and in first-seen order, so the /donate route can warn about sections it skipped. Advisory and never build-failing: the CMS renders kind as a select now, but the Zod schema stays free text on purpose, so a value that predates an option, or arrives from a hand-edited file or a scenario seed, costs one section and a log line rather than the whole deploy. Its sibling goalMetersMissingWidgetId covers the other half of the same problem: a section of the RIGHT kind whose own field is unfilled.
name: unknownSectionKinds

description: Returns the distinct chapter tags on a list of events that match no id in the given chapter list, in first-seen order. The chapters route links an event to its chapter by exact string match on the chapter id, and the CMS renders the chapter field as a free-text box, so a city name instead of a slug or a stray trailing space drops the event off every chapter page while the entry still validates, the build still succeeds, and the events page still lists it. Naming those tags is the only signal an editor gets until the CMS offers a chapter picker. Events with no tag, or a blank one, are excluded rather than reported: an untagged event belongs to no chapter on purpose.
name: unmatchedChapterTags

description: Returns the nav urls with no page behind them, given the routes the site actually builds — the static pages plus what the slug routes generate from published content. Each url is reduced to the page it lands on first: any fragment is dropped so an anchor link resolves against its page and a bare hash resolves against the home page, and a trailing slash is ignored so an editor typing a slash gets no false alarm. This guards the links that stay hand-authored in nav.json now that the chapters are derived — most sharply Content Hub's Blog entry, which points at one specific post and breaks the moment that post is drafted, renamed, or deleted. Deliberately surfaced as a unit test rather than a build gate: the deploy workflow runs the build and never runs vitest, so a dead link informs developers without ever blocking an editor's publish.
name: unresolvedNavUrls

description: Tracks the CMS sign-in session for the runbook's tick controls, hydration-safely. Every render starts signed-out and adopts the real session in an effect after mount: the store answers signed-out on the server and, inside the codeyam preview, signed-in in the browser, so seeding state from it directly rendered two different trees and React discarded the subtree. Accepts an initialSession to pin a fixed session, the seam a scenario uses to capture the signed-out and signed-in states without a token.
name: useAuthSession

untestabilityReason.justification: A React hook over the CMS package's localStorage-backed session store and its window event subscription. Its observable behaviour — which branch of each tick control renders — is covered by the runbook's signed-out and signed-in component scenarios.

description: The photos a gallery shows before and after its 'Show all N photos' control: the first `cap` when collapsed, everything when expanded or when no cap is given. The absent-cap case is what keeps the landing page's 40-photo wall uncapped — a default cap would silently truncate it. Pure; the caller renders from the result and its input is never mutated.
name: visibleGalleryPhotos

description: Prefixes an internal absolute path with import.meta.env.BASE_URL so links resolve under either the domain root (custom domain, base /) or a project subpath (user.github.io/<repo>). External URLs, mailto, and bare hash anchors pass through untouched. Used by the header nav/logo, chapter back link, 404, and blog links for GitHub Pages deployment.
name: withBase

description: Returns a new top-level menu with the derived Chapters dropdown inserted directly after the item labelled Programs, reproducing today's menu order, and appended when no such item exists so a rename or deletion in the CMS degrades sensibly instead of throwing or dropping the group. With no chapter items the group is omitted entirely rather than rendered as an empty dropdown — an empty dropdown is a caret opening onto nothing, and the CMS nav serializer collapses one back into a plain link pointing nowhere. Injecting the group here rather than marking it in nav.json is deliberate: the CMS rebuilds every nav item from label plus children/url and silently drops any other key, so a marker would not survive the first save from the settings editor. Does not mutate the caller's list.
name: withChapterGroup

description: The top-level menu with the derived community links merged into the existing Communities group, after whatever that group already lists by hand. This is the deliberate asymmetry with withChapterGroup: Chapters is a group this module owns and injects wholesale, while Communities is a group an editor already owns in nav.json (the WhatsApp link), so derived items are appended to its children rather than replacing them. With no communities the menu is returned unchanged — including not creating an absent group, since an empty dropdown is the same caret-onto-nothing the chapters rule avoids. Copies the group rather than mutating it, because the layout passes the shared nav.items singleton straight in.
name: withCommunityItems

description: The menu with every link to a hidden homepage band removed, and any dropdown left empty by that removal removed with it. The second half of hiding a section: the same rule that already keeps the derived Chapters and Communities groups honest, applied to the hand-authored anchors in nav.json, so an editor who takes a band off the page is never left with a menu item that scrolls to nothing.
name: withoutHiddenSections
